items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I think Anne Hampton Calloway is one of the coolest women I’ve worked with, you know.

ctx.x: I’m also wondering, is there — I’m trying to think how to phrase this question — do you have to be careful of sending the spotlight towards you?

You know there is, a lot of times, and a lot of singers, in fact most singers, that don’t want me on the bandstand with them. And it’s nothing about music. They don’t want any attention away from what they’re doing, from themselves. So having another woman onstage some would feel is a distraction to them. God forbid it’s another woman. It’s just the way it is. So there are a few exceptions to that. I think Anne Hampton Calloway is one of the coolest women I’ve worked with, you know. She doesn’t care. She’s just…

only put it down to that fact, it’s like why have another woman on stage if I can have X Y Z of guy bass players that won’t take attention away from — not that I’m trying to. If the gig is just me accompanying, I’m just in the background doing my work, you know? But it’s just the way it’s perceived from a woman’s point of view you know. But so the sex situation, I’m really, I’m just happy to play with good people. There’s also a lot of people that just wouldn’t hire a girl musician, for whatever reason, still.
